walkthroughs.body_html:
A feral child grows up without normal human contact.

Sad cases through history show: such children struggle with language, empathy and rules.

In 1970 Los Angeles, 'Genie' was found, aged 13, after years locked alone.

She could barely speak. Despite teaching, she never fully caught up — suggesting a critical period for language.

Sociologists conclude:

  • Humans are made, not just born.
  • Socialisation is essential.
  • Some skills must be learned early.

Family and community truly shape us. ❤️

What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.
Material deprivation is about a lack of clothing; cultural deprivation is about not visiting museums.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between material and cultural deprivation?
options: Material and cultural deprivation are two names for the same poverty.

Material deprivation refers to lack of physical/economic resources (housing, books, food); cultural deprivation refers to lack of skills, values and norms (e.g. parental attitudes to education) that are claimed to support achievement.

options: Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.

By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.
